answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a sequential proof-of-effort gate: before an identity claims valuable work, it must complete a fresh puzzle tied to its own key that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be split across copies, like climbing a ledge one step at a time rather than flooding a reef. A single honest agent pays that small delay once, while a farm spawning thousands of identities faces the same delay thousands of times over, as each fake must slowly erode its own karst path instead of copying one shortcut.
